title: Renaissance Networks and Continuity
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
The word Renaissance suggests rebirth, but no civilization wakes after a perfectly empty night. From roughly the fourteenth to the sixteenth century, scholars and artists in parts of Europe studied Greek and Roman works with new intensity. Yet they did so through manuscripts preserved, copied, translated, and debated during earlier centuries, including work transmitted through Byzantine and Islamic scholarly networks. Renewal therefore meant rearranging inherited materials, not creating knowledge from nothing.

Italian cities provided unusually dense connections among merchants, courts, religious institutions, workshops, and educated readers. Wealthy patrons commissioned buildings, paintings, and books for devotion, civic identity, family memory, and prestige. Patronage gave artists resources, but it also imposed subjects, deadlines, and political expectations. A celebrated name on a work did not erase the assistants, craft traditions, and material suppliers that made production possible.

Artists investigated perspective, light, anatomy, and proportion, sometimes joining visual practice to mathematical or medical inquiry. Observation mattered, but it did not simply replace religion. Sacred subjects remained central, while new techniques changed how bodies, spaces, and narratives were represented. The useful contrast is not faith versus reason; it is a changing relationship among authority, evidence, skill, and interpretation.

Printing accelerated the reproduction of texts and images, but a press did not automatically make information true or equally accessible. Editors selected versions, printers made errors, states and churches censored works, and literacy remained uneven. The Renaissance is best understood as a set of overlapping transformations whose pace differed by place. Its importance lies less in a clean break than in the widening circulation and recombination of people, objects, methods, and arguments.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Renaissance thinkers rejected every medieval source.

options.label: B
options.text: The Renaissance was a networked reorganization of inherited knowledge and practice.

options.label: C
options.text: Printing immediately made accurate knowledge universal.

options.label: D
options.text: Religion disappeared when observation became important.

questions.answer: 正解：B。本文は保存・翻訳された知識、都市ネットワーク、後援、工房、観察、印刷を通じた継承物の再編として説明します。Aは伝承を、Cは印刷の限界を、Dは宗教主題の継続を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage reject the idea that Renaissance revival created knowledge from nothing?

options.label: A
options.text: Classical works and techniques had been preserved, copied, translated, and debated through earlier Byzantine, Islamic, and European networks.

options.label: B
options.text: No Greek or Roman material survived before the fourteenth century.

options.label: C
options.text: Revival meant that scholars stopped rearranging inherited material.

options.label: D
options.text: Printing had already made every ancient text universally available and error-free.

questions.answer: 正解：A。古典資料は前代を通じて保存・翻訳・討論されており、revivalは関心と配置の更新です。B～Dは継承経路を消したり、印刷の時期と効果を誇張したりします。

questions.prompt: The phrase “dense connections” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: many closely linked relationships

options.label: B
options.text: physically heavy buildings

options.label: C
options.text: secret religious rules

options.label: D
options.text: poorly written manuscripts

questions.answer: 正解：A。ここでdenseは商人、宮廷、宗教組織、工房、読者が高密度に結ばれた関係を表します。物理的な重さや文書の質ではありません。

questions.prompt: How did patronage both enable and constrain artists?

options.label: A
options.text: It supplied money, commissions, and visibility while imposing subjects, deadlines, and religious or political expectations.

options.label: B
options.text: It provided complete autonomy and removed every deadline.

options.label: C
options.text: It eliminated the need for workshops, assistants, and material suppliers.

options.label: D
options.text: It prevented patrons from using art for devotion, memory, identity, or prestige.

questions.answer: 正解：A。後援は制作資源と注文、可視性を与える一方、主題・期限・政治宗教的期待を課しました。支援と完全な自律は同義でなく、B～Dは本文と逆です。

questions.prompt: Why does the passage consider “faith versus reason” an inadequate description?

options.label: A
options.text: Sacred subjects continued while observation and mathematical techniques developed, so the relationship among authority, evidence, skill, and interpretation changed rather than one side simply replacing the other.

options.label: B
options.text: Religion vanished as soon as artists studied anatomy.

options.label: C
options.text: Observation played no role in artistic practice.

options.label: D
options.text: Mathematics and religious art could never appear in the same period.

questions.answer: 正解：A。宗教主題が中心に残る一方で観察や数学的技法が発達したため、片方が他方を消したのではなく、知の基準同士の関係が再編されました。B～Dは誤った二項対立です。

questions.prompt: Which inference is best supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Famous artists always worked alone.

options.label: B
options.text: Printing removed selection, error, and censorship.

options.label: C
options.text: Sacred art could coexist with new observational techniques.

options.label: D
options.text: Every European region changed at the same speed.

questions.answer: 正解：C。本文は宗教主題の継続と新しい観察・表現技法の併存を述べます。Aは工房と供給者、Bは編集・誤植・検閲、Dは地域ごとの速度差を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why is urban wealth alone insufficient to explain artistic innovation?

options.label: A
options.text: Resources had to interact with workshop skills, inherited texts, materials, readers, competition, and religious and political institutions.

options.label: B
options.text: Wealth never supplied commissions or production resources.

options.label: C
options.text: Artists required no patrons, materials, or audiences.

options.label: D
options.text: All innovation occurred outside cities without institutional connections.

questions.answer: 正解：A。富は需要と資源を生む一条件ですが、工房技能、資料、材料、読者、競争、制度とのネットワークが制作を可能にしました。B～Dは富の役割を全面否定するか他要因を消します。

questions.prompt: What reasoning does “therefore” express in the sentence about rearranging inherited materials?

options.label: A
options.text: Because earlier centuries preserved, translated, and debated classical materials, renewal is concluded to be their reorganization rather than creation from nothing.

options.label: B
options.text: Because no earlier material existed, renewal must have begun from an empty past.

options.label: C
options.text: Because printing was flawless, inherited materials required no selection.

options.label: D
options.text: Because the Renaissance was uniform, no regional comparison is needed.

questions.answer: 正解：A。「したがって再生とは、無から知識を作ることではなく、受け継いだ材料を組み直すことだった」。thereforeは保存・翻訳・討論という根拠から再生の意味を限定する結論へ進みます。

questions.prompt: Which revision best corrects the claim that the Renaissance completely rejected the Middle Ages and invented modernity?

options.label: A
options.text: It intensified and reorganized inherited texts, techniques, patronage, observation, and circulation through overlapping networks, with uneven change across regions rather than one complete break.

options.label: B
options.text: It destroyed every medieval institution and recovered knowledge without any Byzantine or Islamic transmission.

options.label: C
options.text: It was a single moment when printing instantly created universal truth.

options.label: D
options.text: It introduced observation only after religious art had disappeared entirely.

questions.answer: 正解：A。中世の写本・翻訳・宗教機関とビザンツ・イスラム圏の伝承を踏まえ、強度と組合せ、流通が地域ごとに変化したと直すのが妥当です。B～Dは断絶を過度に単純化します。
